prose.label: Which attribute is the identity.
prose.text: The user ID rules are in [[zia.ad-integration.identity-objects]], and the domain in the login must be registered as described in [[zia.scim.setup]]. {{login-from-username-only}}

prose.label: Department.
prose.text: {{enterprise-department}} {{connector-omits-department}} {{department-per-idp}} The Entra ID and Google Workspace guides write the department attribute path differently {{divergence:department-attribute-path}}. Whether the string must match an existing department is a separate question: [[zia.scim.groups-and-departments]].

Three points are open: which attributes are required {{gap:required-attributes}}, whether custom attributes are persisted {{gap:custom-attributes}}, and how the remaining IdPs handle department by default {{gap:per-idp-department-mapping}}.

user-fields.statement: ZIA maps these SCIM user attributes: id to a Zscaler-generated unique ID; externalId to scim_externalid; userName to the user ID (login_name) in user@domain form; displayName to the display name (user_name); groups to Groups; active to enabled or disabled; department to Department; name.givenName and name.familyName to first and last name; emails.value to scim_emails.

quotes: | id | <unique_id> | Unique ID generated by Zscaler. For example, 1a234567-1b23-1200-1234-123c |
| externalId | scim_externalid | External ID provided by the client populates onto the Zscaler user database |
The actual user ID used for authentication. The expected format is user@domain.
| displayName | User display Name (user_name) | The display name of the user |
| groups | Groups | The Groups the user belongs to |
| department | Department | The department the user belongs to |
| name.givenName | firstname | The first name of the user |
| name.familyName | lastname | The last name of the user |
When "active=false," Zscaler disables this user When "active=true," Zscaler enables this user
| emails.value | scim_emails | The email address of the user |

group-fields.statement: ZIA maps these SCIM group attributes: id to a Zscaler-generated unique ID, externalId to scim_externalid (kept in the Zscaler database), and displayName to the group Name.

quotes: | externalId | scim_externalid | External ID provided by the client that is kept in the Zscaler database |
| displayName | Name | Display name of the Group |
| id | <unique_id> | Unique ID generated by Zscaler.

name-prefix.statement: ZIA's SCIM name attributes use the singular prefix name. (name.givenName, name.familyName); the ZPA mapping uses names.givenName.

quotes: | name.givenName | firstname | The first name of the user |
| name.familyName | lastname | The last name of the user |
| First Name | names.givenName | The first name of the user |

enterprise-department.statement: In Zscaler's create and update examples the department is sent inside the enterprise user extension (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User), and the Go SDK models it as the `Department` field of an `EnterpriseUser` struct held in the SCIM user's enterprise extension field.

quotes: # Updating a User's Display Name and Department
type SCIMUser struct { Schemas []string `json:"schemas,omitempty"` ID string `json:"id,omitempty"` UserName string `json:"userName,omitempty"` DisplayName string `json:"displayName,omitempty"`

connector-omits-department.statement: A SCIM connector that sends only the core user schema, without the enterprise extension, sends no department, so the ZIA user has an empty department and department-scoped rules do not match that user.
connector-omits-department.conditions: Derived from the department being carried in the extension; whether a given connector emits the extension by default is not captured, and the consequence for rules follows from the user record lacking the value.

login-from-username-only.statement: Only the SCIM userName attribute maps to the ZIA login name; externalId and emails.value map to the reference fields scim_externalid and scim_emails.
login-from-username-only.conditions: Reads the mapping list as complete: no other attribute is mapped to login_name.

department-per-idp.statement: In the PingOne guide's SCIM attribute table Department maps to department. In the Entra ID guide the table maps the enterprise-extension department attribute to department.

entra-scim-mappings.statement: The Entra ID guide's mapping tables send, for users, userPrincipalName to userName, objectId to externalId, the expression Switch([IsSoftDeleted], , "False", "True", "True", "False") to active, surname to name.familyName, givenName to name.givenName and displayName to displayName; for groups, displayName to displayName, members to members and objectId to externalId.

pingone-google-scim-mappings.statement: The PingOne guide maps Enabled to active, Family Name to familyName, Given Name to givenName, Username to userName and Email Address to workEmail, and builds displayName from the expression user.name.given + " " + user.name.family. The Google Workspace guide maps Formatted name to displayName, Last name to name.familyName, First name to name.givenName and Username to userName.

quotes: Click the Advanced Expression icon for the displayName attribute.
19. In the Build and Test Expression window, enter user.name.given + " " + user.name.family.

workflow-automation-attributes.statement: Where the Workflow Automation Admin Portal is used, the Entra ID and Okta guides add user attributes beyond the core mapping, for example the enterprise-extension manager.value, employeeNumber and mobile phoneNumbers in Entra ID, and manager and employeeNumber in Okta. The guides add them for Workflow Automation; whether ZIA itself stores them is not stated.

quotes: (Optional) If you use the Workflow Automation Admin Portal, add and map additional user attributes that Workflow Automation uses.

department-attribute-path.summary: The Entra ID and Google Workspace guides write the enterprise-extension department attribute with a colon and with a dot before department.

positions.says: The Entra ID table maps urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:department (a colon before department) to department.
The Google Workspace table maps Department to urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User.department (a dot before department).

department-attribute-path.impact: The enterprise-department claim's create and update examples put department inside the enterprise extension object, which matches neither notation literally. The dot may be the Google console's notation for the same target; the guides do not say, so do not tell an operator which path string to type for a custom connector.

required-attributes.title: Which SCIM attributes ZIA requires
required-attributes.detail: Unverified legacy statement: The vendor doc marks only userName as required, and groups or department are needed for identity-aware policy. The captured SCIM article has no required column; Zscaler's create example sends schemas, userName, displayName and the department extension. A schema read from /Schemas on a tenant, or a vendor statement, would settle it.
required-attributes.blocks: telling an IdP admin which attributes are mandatory

custom-attributes.title: Whether ZIA persists attributes outside the documented mapping
custom-attributes.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Custom SCIM attributes beyond the documented mapping are not persisted in ZIA, and the multi-valued attributes are groups and emails.value with all others single-valued. This was inferred from the ZPA article's explicit custom-attribute limitation; the ZIA article lists only the mapping above. A push of an unmapped attribute and a read-back would settle it.
custom-attributes.blocks: answering whether a custom IdP attribute can drive ZIA policy

per-idp-department-mapping.title: How each IdP maps or omits the department attribute by default
per-idp-department-mapping.detail: The Entra ID, PingOne and Okta guides' department mappings are now sourced (department-per-idp), with the Google Workspace notation in divergence department-attribute-path; the Okta table is in the guide's optional Workflow Automation attributes. The PingFederate guide defers configuration to PingFederate's documentation, so its department handling is not in any captured source (former ledger zia-43), and whether each connector sends department out of the box is not stated.
per-idp-department-mapping.blocks: telling operators whether their connector sends department out of the box
